title: Split StateManager.ts task/worker/chat concerns into modules
description: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts is 3600+ lines mixing task lifecycle, worker lifecycle, chat/channels, proposals, and persistence. Extract cohesive modules (behavior-preserving moves with re-exports from StateManager) one concern per task if needed. Coordinate around in-flight governance-plane-v2 edits — rebase, do not conflict.
definitionOfDone: extracted modules have focused names and no circular imports
full vitest suite passes with zero regressions

implementationPlan.description: EXTRACT validators.ts. Also move the constants MAX_COMMENTS_PER_TASK_DEFAULT / MAX_COMMENTS_PER_TASK_ENV / MAX_COMMENTS_PER_TASK (re-export MAX_COMMENTS_PER_TASK from StateManager.ts — it is already exported and external code may import it) and ACTIVITY_TEXT_PREVIEW_CHARS / ACTIVITY_TRUNCATED_SUFFIX plus the activityStringPreview helper. The ONLY signature change: validateSettingsUpdate takes the current project explicitly — `validateSettingsUpdate(project: Project, settings: Partial<ProjectSettings>): ProjectSettings` — because it reads this.project. Every other function is pure and takes no state handle. These are all private helpers, so there are NO delegation stubs: rewrite each call site inside StateManager.ts to call the imported function directly. implementationPlan.description: EXTRACT persistence.ts. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/state/persistence.ts holding the disk-IO, bootstrap and migration layer. Move: loadEntities, readJson, writeEntity, verifyWritePermissions, normalizeProject, migrateToV5FileSystem, migrateToV6FileSystem, ensureChatInfrastructure, ensureRoleChannels, seedCanonicalChannel, tryLoadWorkerFromDisk. Signature rules: pure path helpers take the path explicitly — `loadEntities<T>(moePath: string, dir: string): Map<string, T>`, `readJson<T>(filePath: string): T`, `normalizeProject(project: Partial<Project>): Project`, `verifyWritePermissions(moePath: string): void`; anything that mutates in-memory maps or consults the FileWatcher takes the state handle first — `writeEntity(state: StateManager, kind: string, id: string, entity: unknown): Promise<void>`, `migrateToV5FileSystem(state)`, `migrateToV6FileSystem(state)`, `ensureChatInfrastructure(state)`, `ensureRoleChannels(state)`, `seedCanonicalChannel(state, name, type)`, `tryLoadWorkerFromDisk(state, workerId)`. Preserve writeEntity's path-traversal guard (validateEntityId + the resolved-path startsWith check) and its fileWatcher.ignorePath call in the same order — that ordering is what stops the watcher echoing our own writes. Error handling is load-bearing here and must move verbatim: loadEntities skips and logs an unparseable entity file instead of aborting the whole load, and tryLoadWorkerFromDisk swallows every throw and returns null by design — do not 'improve' either into a propagating error. tryLoadWorkerFromDisk is PUBLIC: keep a one-line delegating method on StateManager. `load()` and `applySettingsTimeouts` STAY in StateManager as the orchestrator; rewrite their internals to call the imported functions. Verify tsc = 0 and suite = baseline.
implementationPlan.note:
Created src/state/persistence.ts (370 lines) with all 11 disk-IO/bootstrap/migration functions moved verbatim; load() and applySettingsTimeouts stay in StateManager as the orchestrator and now call the imported functions. StateManager.ts 3213 → 2900 lines. tsc 0, suite 55 files / 863 tests = baseline.

Signatures follow the plan's RULE (pure path helpers take paths; anything touching in-memory maps or the FileWatcher takes the state handle), which in three cases means a narrower signature than the plan's illustrative example — documented rather than silently deviated: loadEntities keeps `(dir: string)` because its body only ever uses the full `dir` path, so an added moePath param would be dead weight; normalizeProject needs `(projectPath: string, project)` because its body reads this.projectPath for the default project name; migrateToV5FileSystem/migrateToV6FileSystem take `(moePath: string)` since they touch only the filesystem, never the maps. ensureChatInfrastructure/ensureRoleChannels/seedCanonicalChannel/tryLoadWorkerFromDisk/writeEntity take the state handle as specified. persistence.ts also needed atomicWriteJson (not just the Async variant), which the plan did not list.

Preserved as required: writeEntity's validateEntityId → resolved-path prefix check → fileWatcher.ignorePath → write ordering; loadEntities' skip-and-log on an unparseable entity file; tryLoadWorkerFromDisk's swallow-everything-return-null; verifyWritePermissions still throws (an unwritable .moe must be fatal at startup).

PLAN CORRECTION worth flagging for QA: the planning notes asserted "no test in the repo reaches StateManager privates". That is false — StateManager.test.ts has two tests that `vi.spyOn(stateManager as unknown as { writeEntity }, 'writeEntity')` to simulate a failed disk write, and they went red the moment writeEntity stopped being an instance method. Rather than edit a test file (which the plan says would blow the 10-file budget and require report_blocked), I kept writeEntity as a public delegating method and reverted all 18 internal call sites to `this.writeEntity(...)` so the spy still intercepts — behavior-preserving, budget-compliant, and the stub carries a comment explaining why it must stay a method. tryLoadWorkerFromDisk also has a delegating stub (chatJoin.ts and chatSend.ts call it).

THREE CORRECTIONS, each caught by a failing check rather than assumed away:
1. getMessageMutex STAYED on StateManager. It is the only chat function needing the AsyncMutex constructor, and importing that from chatStore would have converted the intended type-only edge into a real runtime import cycle — precisely what step-10's guard exists to catch. chatStore now calls state.getMessageMutex(channelId), so mutex identity is unchanged and the runtime graph stays one-way. (AsyncMutex is now exported from StateManager for typing only.)
2. My first pass hand-wrote the delegating stubs and got several signatures wrong (getMessages, getUnreadSummary, pinMessage, createDecision, approveDecision, rejectDecision) — tsc caught 10 arity/shape errors, and this is exactly the drift the plan forbids. I replaced them with stubs GENERATED from the extracted functions' own signatures (scratchpad/gen_stubs.py), so drift is impossible by construction rather than by care.
3. Behavioural, not just structural: converting moved-to-moved calls into direct module calls changed dispatch. postSystemMessage originally called `this.postToGeneral(...)`, which an instance spy intercepts; a direct call bypassed it and broke reportBlocked.test.ts's assertion that the general channel receives two posts. Calls between PUBLIC chat functions now go through `state.` so the original virtual dispatch is preserved, with a comment in the module explaining why. Same root cause as step-3's writeEntity finding — worth watching in every remaining extraction.

implementationPlan.description: EXTRACT sweeps.ts — the timer/watcher layer. Preserve the alertedStaleAssignments dedupe set semantics via state.alertedStaleAssignments. implementationPlan.description: ADD THE DoD GUARD TEST. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/state/stateModules.test.ts with three vitest cases, using only node:fs / node:path (no new dependency — madge and dpdm are deliberately not added). (1) 'StateManager.ts stays under the size budget': read the file, assert its line count is < 1500 with a message naming the actual count, so the number regresses loudly rather than silently. (2) 'no runtime import cycles inside src/state': glob src/state/*.ts excluding *.test.ts, extract only RUNTIME relative imports and build a directed graph, then DFS for a cycle and assert none, printing the offending path on failure. The extractor MUST skip type-only imports — both whole-clause `import type { X } from './y.js'` and inline `import { type X } from './y.js'` specifiers — because every extracted module does `import type { StateManager }` while StateManager imports the module for real; that type-level cycle is erased at compile time and is the intended design, so counting it fails the test by construction. Scope the graph to src/state/** only: StateManager already imports ../tools/submitPlan.js and ../tools/waitForTask.js, a pre-existing cross-directory edge this task does not own. Give the file-reading helper real error handling — a path that disappears mid-scan should fail the assertion with the offending filename, not throw a bare ENOENT out of the test body. (3) 'every extracted module is reachable and named for one concern': assert the eight expected module files exist (validators, persistence, activityLog, chatStore, teamStore, sweeps, taskStore, workerStore) so a future merge that deletes or renames one trips here.
